scientific_rubric.description: Identity and scope: Retain the full molecular connectivity, 165-atom composition and neutral charge. Document any candidate electron/spin state and show raw evidence that it exists or collapses. Distinguish formal oxidation-state accounting, orbital composition, spin density and atomic population charges; none is interchangeable with the others.

Quantitative scientific results: Provide quantitative, state-resolved electronic evidence and the corresponding molecular/state validation. If alternative initializations collapse, preserve the raw convergence/state evidence and describe what was actually tested.

Evidence that distinguishes the claimed explanation: Support the chosen electronic/bonding account using mutually informative evidence and explain why alternatives are retained, rejected or unresolved. The investigator chooses candidates and methods; no three-state or two-functional matrix is mandatory.

Uncertainty and limits: Evaluate dependence of the conclusion on electronic representation, numerical reliability and geometry as appropriate. Preserve the distinction between a robust state assignment and an ambiguous covalency interpretation.

Bounded answer to the question: Deliver a substantiated electronic-state and bonding description with limits; supported alternative descriptions or unresolved physical oxidation are acceptable. Merely repeating the formal Ni(IV) label or old triplet gap earns no complete result credit.

scoring_notes: AR and PR share result validity; actual open_research runtime supplies mode-specific process rubrics.
Source author outcomes are conditional reference evidence, not mandatory winners. No inherited numerical tolerance.
No penalty simply for a different justified model, hypothesis count, metric or valid analysis route. Scientific adequacy is claim-dependent.
Completion requires a substantiated answer to the stated question. Honest partial credit is distinct from passing all scientific criteria.
